references.text: Describes the original event at Sinai/Horeb where the people experienced thunder, lightning, a trumpet blast, and smoke, and they asked Moses to speak to them instead of God.
The people saw the thunder and lightning and heard the trumpet blast, and they asked Moses to speak to them because they feared dying if God spoke directly to them.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord spoke with them face to face on the mountain, out of the fire.
A parallel account where the people ask Moses to be their mediator because they feared the great fire and that they would die if they continued to hear the voice of the Lord.
Refers to the day of assembly when the Lord spoke out of the fire on the mountain.
Mentions again the day of assembly on the mountain when the Ten Commandments were given out of the fire.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to this event and describes how the Israelites came to a mountain with fire, darkness, storm, and trumpet sounds, and they asked that no more word be spoken to them.
